proposed.explanation: While a physical object might manifest as a point visually, the point itself is conceptual. A circle is a shape; a point is the center or organizing focus. While survey points mark locations, Ching's point is a spatial organizing element, not a measurement tool. A point is a conceptual tool with no length, width, or depth. It marks position. In architecture, we perceive points as convergences of lines, junctures of planes, or single objects creating visual centers that organize surrounding space.
